svg.text: One search run per (dataset, seed, budget). Left: the loop as implemented in archtree/search.py. Middle: what supports and evaluates it. Right: each block in plain terms.
proposes candidate t: value + C·√(ln N / n)
store accuracy in the trie node
next iteration t + 1, until the budget is spent
real evaluations, GPU-hours; TCR / TCR-H logged
Each iteration, walks the tree of design choices to propose one new architecture.
After 10 real tests, half the time swaps that proposal for a tweak of a top design.
An AI model guesses which branches look promising. Studied separately; off in the main
The tree remembers every design, so no design is ever paid for twice.
A one-pass check on an untrained network; only the top 35% go on to a real test.
Three training-free scores averaged with equal weight. Needs no accuracy labels.
Looks up the design's accuracy — the expensive step the pipeline tries to minimise.
Feeds the result back up the tree so future choices get smarter.
Lets a child reuse its parent's weights. Simulated here, since nothing is trained.
Every 50 steps, cuts the weakest 15% of branches so the search stays focused.
Picks the best design on validation data and reports its test accuracy and cost.
How much of the space was covered; TCR-H also rewards good accuracy–latency trade-offs.
Rotates several API keys so rate limits never stall the LLM studies.
Every answer, score and result is saved safely, so nothing is recomputed or lost.
A stopped pipeline restarts where it left off.
Compare against other methods, and switch one part off at a time to prove it helps.
Tests if differences are real (Wilcoxon, Holm), ranks methods (Friedman) and checks
